concepts.name: Perimeter
concepts.description: The perimeter of a closed figure is the total length of its boundary. Students explore perimeter by measuring the sides of regular and irregular shapes.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the perimeter of simple closed figures by adding the lengths of all sides.

concepts.name: Measuring Boundary Length
concepts.description: Boundary length can be measured using rulers, strings, or grids. Students compare the boundaries of different shapes through practical activities.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to measure and compare the boundary lengths of different shapes.

concepts.name: Units of Perimeter
concepts.description: Perimeter is measured using units of length such as centimetres and metres. Choosing the appropriate unit depends on the size of the object.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to express perimeter using appropriate units of measurement.

concepts.name: Area as Surface Coverage
concepts.description: Area measures the amount of surface covered by a shape. Students understand area by covering figures with equal-sized square units.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain area as the amount of surface covered by a shape.

concepts.name: Square Units
concepts.description: Square units provide a standard method for measuring area. Students estimate and calculate area by counting unit squares.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine the area of simple figures using square units.

concepts.name: Comparing Areas
concepts.description: Different shapes may have the same area even if their boundaries differ. Students compare figures to understand this relationship.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compare the areas of different shapes using unit squares.

concepts.name: Difference Between Area and Perimeter
concepts.description: Perimeter measures the boundary of a figure, while area measures the space inside it. These two measurements describe different properties of a shape.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish between area and perimeter in practical situations.

concepts.name: Comparing Shapes
concepts.description: Shapes with equal perimeters can have different areas, and shapes with equal areas can have different perimeters.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to compare shapes based on both area and perimeter.

concepts.name: Practical Applications
concepts.description: Area and perimeter are used in planning gardens, fencing fields, tiling floors, and designing rooms.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve everyday problems involving area and perimeter.

concepts.name: Estimation Using Grids
concepts.description: Students estimate the area of irregular shapes by counting complete and partial squares on a grid.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to estimate the area of irregular figures using grid methods.

concepts.name: Measuring Regular Shapes
concepts.description: Regular shapes can be measured accurately using square units and simple counting strategies.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the area of regular figures using square units.

concepts.name: Reasonableness of Measurement
concepts.description: Students verify their measurements by comparing estimates with calculated values and checking for accuracy.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to evaluate whether measured areas and perimeters are reasonable.

concepts.name: Understanding Area and Boundary
concepts.description: This chapter develops students' understanding of perimeter, area, square units, and the relationship between boundary length and surface coverage through practical measurement activities.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to measure, compare, and apply the concepts of area and perimeter to solve real-life mathematical problems.
